source.title: $\textit{New News}$: System-2 Fine-tuning for Robust Integration of New Knowledge
source.authors: Core Francisco Park; Zechen Zhang; Hidenori Tanaka

record.file_problem: None noted; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper examines scaling during a distinct fine-tuning regime and reports that the compute-related trend it observes in evaluation accuracy does not appear in training loss.
record.gate_note: The study cites the original scaling-law papers as background, but does not reproduce their held-out pretraining-loss sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute. The scaling-related results are limited to Sys2-FT on the New News math split: evaluation accuracy versus fine-tuning compute, and training loss versus fine-tuning compute. Other reported ICL, fine-tuning, and capability results do not measure the claim versions’ scaling behavior.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its 'emerging scaling law' is a qualitative observation: Self-QA fine-tuning accuracy on the New News math split roughly collapses across 3B+ Qwen2.5 models when plotted against fine-tuning compute. No power law is fitted. No held-out loss is measured. Pretraining size, tokens and compute are not varied. The fine-tuning training loss (Fig. 10b) is computed on self-generated data that differs across model sizes, and the authors say the missing trend there is expected for that reason. The original scaling-law papers are not cited. The 'scaling law' label refers to a different construct, fine-tuning sample-efficiency in task accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report preliminary evidence that, for sufficiently large models (3B+), Self-QA fine-tuning accuracy follows a compute-dependent relation, suggesting larger models are more sample-efficient. Its generality across datasets and sizes is unclear. They say the relation's absence in training loss is expected because the training data differ across model sizes; it is not presented as a negative finding.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fine-tuning study using Self-QA-generated data and downstream task accuracy or fine-tuning training loss, rather than pretraining runs measuring held-out loss across parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy trend is limited to the New News math subset and Self-QA protocol; the authors state that smaller models do not join the accuracy curve even when given FLOPs matched to the 14B run.

fits_no_version.finding: On the New News math split with Self-QA fine-tuning, Qwen2.5 models of 3B and above reach similar accuracy at equal fine-tuning compute. The 0.5B and 1.5B models stay below that curve even with FLOPs matched to the 14B run. Fine-tuning training loss shows no such collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For self-generated QA fine-tuning, task accuracy depends mainly on fine-tuning compute above a model-size threshold, implying larger models are more sample-efficient.

record.code_released: Code, data and model checkpoints will be available after the review process; URL not stated.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is preliminary and limited to fine-tuning the New News math subset with Self-QA. Scaling-curve values are shown in figures rather than stated numerically in the text, and uncertainty for the scaling results is not stated. The authors note that training data differ across model sizes and that the extent of the accuracy trend across datasets and model sizes is unclear.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows retained for the claim: the paper's other domain, protocol, ICL, capability-preservation, and continual-learning results do not measure the scaling-law versions. Figures 4 and 10a include task-accuracy comparisons, but only the compute-dependent math Self-QA result is catalogued here; its figure-only values are summarized in r2.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining-loss sweeps over parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted laws and no extrapolation.
No comparison of model shape at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit for the fine-tuning regime. Accuracy-vs-compute collapse is shown only qualitatively, and loss is on size-dependent training data.
Downstream accuracy is not related to pretraining scale or pretraining loss. Bigger models doing better after Sys2-FT (Fig. 4b) is not a predictability test.
No comparison of fitting or setup choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label for V5 is removed. Row r1 is not held-out loss and no power law was tested, so it cannot challenge the power-law form. The paper's main contributions (the New News dataset, Sys2-FT protocols, contextual shadowing, curse of overexposure) are unrelated to the scaling-law claim.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No power laws fitted on small pretraining runs or extrapolations to larger runs.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Only a fine-tuning regime is examined; other modalities, repeated data, transfer, and other fine-tuning settings are not tested.

The paper measures downstream accuracy after deliberately fine-tuning on the evaluation domain; it does not test downstream performance as a predictable consequence of pretraining scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of parameter counting, fitting methods, or other setup choices for the published pretraining scaling laws.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 family (model sizes shown in Fig. 10)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training cross-entropy loss across fine-tuning compute for Self-QA Sys2-FT runs.
rows.note: The authors state that the compute-dependent relation seen in evaluation accuracy does not appear in training loss, noting that the generated training data differs across model sizes. This is fine-tuning training loss, not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: This is fine-tuning training loss on self-generated data that differs by model size, not held-out loss. No power-law fit is attempted. The authors say the absence of a compute relation is expected because the training data differ. It cannot bear on V5's power-law form, so it cannot support a 'challenges' verdict.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 family (model sizes shown in Fig. 10)
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream evaluation accuracy across fine-tuning compute for Self-QA Sys2-FT runs.
rows.measure: New News evaluation accuracy versus fine-tuning compute
rows.note: The authors describe an empirical compute-dependent accuracy relation: models of 3B or larger appear to reach similar evaluation accuracy at the same fine-tuning compute. The text calls this preliminary evidence of greater sample efficiency in larger models. This is fine-tuned task accuracy, not a version’s pretraining-loss or compute-optimal allocation measure.
rows.check: Figure-only collapse of fine-tuned task accuracy against fine-tuning compute. No power-law form is fitted, and it is not a pretraining-scale downstream trend (V6). It is correctly unlinked, but 'observed' has no version to be observed against.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ran a fine-tuning compute-matched comparison with the 14B run.
rows.baseline: 14B run at matched FLOPs; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors state that the small models do not join the accuracy scaling curve even when trained with equal FLOPs.
rows.check: Compute-matched control showing the 0.5B model stays off the accuracy curve. It bears only on the paper's own sample-efficiency observation.
